{{Short description|Scottish writer and schoolmaster (1782–1850)}}
{{EngvarB|date=August 2014}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2020}}
'''Alexander Jamieson''' (1782–1850) was a Scottish writer and schoolmaster, now best known as a [[rhetorician]]. He has been described as effectively a professional textbook writer.<ref name="CarrCarr2005">{{Cite book |author1= Carr, Jean Ferguson |author2= Carr, Stephen L. |author3= Schultz, Lucille M. |title=Archives of Instruction: Nineteenth-Century Rhetorics, Readers, And Composition Books in the United States |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZeJsjnqcPCsC&pg=PA42|year=2005 |publisher= [[SIU Press]] |isbn=978-0-8093-2611-2 |pages=42–3}}</ref> After the failure of his school, he worked as an [[actuary]].<ref name="Ridpath">[https://academic.oup.com/astrogeo/article/54/1/1.22/194362 ''Alexander Jamieson, celestial map maker'', by Ian Ridpath.]</ref>

==Life==
Some of Jamieson's background is obscure.<ref name="Thommes">{{ThoemmesBritish19C|Jamieson, Alexander (fl. 1818)|591}}</ref> He was born at [[Rothesay, Bute]], to William Jamieson, a [[wheelwright]], and Margaret Stewart. In 1821 he obtained a degree of M.A. from [[Marischal College, Aberdeen]], and an LL.D. there in 1823.<ref name="Ridpath"/> In 1825, he was admitted as a [[sizar]] at [[St John's College, Cambridge]], and became a [[ten-year man]].<ref>{{Acad|JMY825A|Jamieson, Alexander}}</ref> In 1826 he became a member of the [[Royal Astronomical Society|Astronomical Society of London]].<ref name="Ridpath"/>

Jamieson was active in the period between 1814 and 1846, writing textbooks and running a school. In 1824, it was teaching at Heston House on [[Hounslow Heath]], where some [[Hindustani language|Hindustani]] was on the syllabus. From 1826 to 1838 it was at [[Wyke House]] Academy in [[Middlesex]], which was advertised as a preparation for the Army, Navy, civil engineers, architects and surveyors.<ref name="Ridpath"/><ref>{{Cite book |editor= Buckingham, James Silk  |editor-link=James Silk Buckingham |title=The Oriental herald and colonial review |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZKsEAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA379|year=1825 |page=379}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |author= Bryant, Margaret Elizabeth |title=The London Experience of Secondary Education |year=1986 |publisher=Athlone |isbn=0485113023 |page=156}}</ref> Among his pupils there was [[George Windsor Earl]];<ref>{{Cite ODNB |id=59850 |title=Earl, George Samuel Windsor |first=R. H. W. |last=Reece}}</ref> [[John Rouse Bloxam]] also taught there.<ref>{{Cite DNBSupp |wstitle=Bloxam, John Rouse}}</ref>

Jamieson was declared bankrupt in 1838.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Comprising Reports of Cases in the Courts of Chancery, King's Bench, and Common Pleas, from 1822 to 1835: And Law Journal Reports Divided into Equity and Bankruptcy Cases. Common Law Cases 1836–1858 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bzNFAAAAYAAJ&pg=RA4-PA14 |year=1838 |page=14}}</ref> He then worked as an actuary. 

Towards the end of his life, he suffered a stroke, then moved to [[Bruges]] in Belgium with his wife, Frances (''née'' Thurtle), known as a writer, whom he had married in 1820. She was the author of the relatively successful ''Ashford Rectory; or, The Spoiled Child Reformed. Containing a short introduction to the sciences of architecture and heraldry...''.<ref>3rd e. corrected and enlarged (London: G. and W. B. Whittaker, 1820). See the bookseller catalogue ''Women Writers R–Z'' (London: Jarndyce, 2012). {{ISBN|9781900718899}}.</ref> He died in Bruges on 6 July 1850.<ref name="Ridpath"/><ref>{{Cite book |author= Urban, Sylvanus |author-link=Sylvanus Urban |title=The Gentleman's Magazine: Historical Chronicle |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-rEUAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA369|year=1820 |page=369}}</ref>

==Works==
Jamieson was the author of two highly successful grammars: ''A Grammar of Rhetoric and Polite Literature'' (1818, at least fifty-three American editions) and ''A Grammar of Logic and Intellectual Philosophy'' (1819 and at least ten American editions).<ref name="Thommes"/> The former drew on [[Hugh Blair]]'s ''Lectures on Rhetoric and Belles Lettres'', and the ''Philosophy of Rhetoric'' of [[George Campbell (minister)|George Campbell]], of which Jamieson published an abridgement in 1823.<ref>{{Cite book |author= Murphy, James J. |title=A Short History of Writing Instruction: From Ancient Greece to Contemporary America |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qdJcE0F34I4C&pg=PA181|year=2012 |publisher= [[Routledge]] |isbn=978-0-415-89745-7 |page=181}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |author1= Campbell, George |author2= Jamieson, Alexander |title=The Philosophy of Rhetoric... Abridged for... Schools |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=b3vFnQEACAAJ|year=1823|publisher=London}}</ref> Jamieson also abridged the ''Elements of Criticism'' by [[Lord Kames]].<ref name="CarrCarr2005"/>

All these Scottish authors, along with [[Alexander Bain (philosopher)|Alexander Bain]], were widely used in 19th-century American colleges for rhetoric texts;<ref>{{Cite book |author1= Gaillet, Lynee Lewis  |author2= Horner, Winifred Bryan |title=The Present State of Scholarship in the History of Rhetoric: A Twenty-First Century Guide |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LLzCBpstRO0C&pg=PA159|year=2010|publisher= [[University of Missouri Press]] |isbn=978-0-8262-7218-8 |page=159}}</ref> and the ''Grammar'' of Jamieson went through 24 editions by 1844.<ref>{{Cite book |author= Zimmerman, Brett |title=Edgar Allan Poe: Rhetoric and Style |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hNn8kKr_L0IC&pg=PA30 |year=2005 |publisher=McGill-Queen's Press – MQUP |isbn=978-0-7735-7291-1 |page=30}}</ref> It quoted freely from [[Joseph Addison]] and [[Mark Akenside]], as well as sources such as Shakespeare and [[John Milton]],<ref>{{Cite book |author= Crowley, Sharon |title=Composition in the University: Historical and Polemical Essays|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cO09M-bXkecC&pg=PA51|year=1998|publisher= [[University of Pittsburgh Press]] |isbn=978-0-8229-7190-0 |page=51}}</ref> and was a typical text of the [[female education]] of the period.<ref>{{Cite book |author1= Hackel, Heidi Brayman |author2= Kelly, Catherine E.  |title=Reading Women: Literacy, Authorship, and Culture in the Atlantic World, 1500–1800 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8mXr8L7asUIC&pg=PA129|year=2008 |publisher=[[University of Pennsylvania Press]] |isbn=978-0-8122-0598-5 |page=129}}</ref> The ''Grammar of Rhetoric'' combined Blair, Campbell, and Kames with the ''Lectures on Belles Lettres and Logic'' (1806) of [[William Barron (historian)|William Barron]] and the grammar of [[Lindley Murray]].<ref name="CarrCarr2005"/>

Other works were:
[[File:Alexander Jamieson Celestial Atlas cover.jpg|thumb|Cover of ''A Celestial Atlas'' by Alexander Jamieson]]
*''A Treatise on the Construction of Maps''<ref name="CarrCarr2005"/><ref>{{Cite book |author= Jamieson, Alexander |title=A Treatise on the Construction of Maps; in which the Principles of the Projections of the Sphere are Demonstrated, and Their Various Practical Relations to Mathematical Geography, Deduced and Explained... with an Appendix... By Alexander Jamieson |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=66xQhUOBpeMC |year=1814 |publisher=for C. Law... etc.!}}</ref>
*''A Grammar of Universal Geography'' (1820?, 1823)<ref>{{Cite book |author= Sitwell, O F G |title=Four Centuries of Special Geography: An Annotated Guide to Books That Purport to Describe All the Countries in the World Published... |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-a4HejRfsyAC&pg=PA327 |year=2011 |publisher= [[UBC Press]] |isbn=978-0-7748-4457-4 |page=327}}</ref>
*''[[A Celestial Atlas]]'' (1822)<ref name="CarrCarr2005"/><ref>{{Cite web |author= Ridpath, Ian |author-link=Ian Ridpath |title=Celestial Atlas by Alexander Jamieson |url=http://www.ianridpath.com/atlases/jamieson.html |access-date=31 July 2013}}</ref> This work was inspired by the [[star atlas]] of [[Johann Elert Bode]], but restricted itself to stars that could be seen with the naked eye. It further inspired ''[[Urania's Mirror]]'', a work that has been attributed to Richard Rouse Bloxam.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Ian Ridpath |title=Urania's Mirror |url=http://www.ianridpath.com/atlases/urania.html |access-date=31 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |author= Kanas, Nick |title=Star Maps: History, Artistry, and Cartography |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bae3LP4tfP4C&pg=PA185|year=2012|publisher=Springer |isbn=978-1-4614-0917-5 |pages=185–6}}</ref>
*''Conversations on General History, exhibiting a Progressive View of the State of Mankind'' (2nd edition 1823)<ref>{{Cite book |author= Jamieson, Alexander |title=Conversations on General History, exhibiting a progressive view of the state of mankind from the earliest ages... to the beginning of the year 1819 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=piVXAAAAcAAJ|year=1823}}</ref>
*''A Dictionary of Mechanical Science, Arts, Manufactures, and Miscellaneous Knowledge'' Volume 1 (1827),<ref name="Alexander Jamieson 1829">{{Cite book |author=Alexander Jamieson |title=A Dictionary of Mechanical Science, Arts, Manufactures, and Miscellaneous Knowledge |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YY61vWR8pQQC |year=1829 |publisher=H. Fisher, Son & Company}}</ref> Volume 2 (1829)<ref name="Alexander Jamieson 1829"/>
*''Mechanics of Fluids for Practical Men'' (1837)<ref name="CarrCarr2005"/><ref>{{Cite book |author= Jamieson, Alexander |title=Mechanics of fluids for practical men: comprising hydrostatics, descriptive and constructive; the whole illustrated by numerous examples and appropriate diagrams |url=https://archive.org/details/mechanicsfluids01jamigoog|access-date=31 July 2013 |year=1837 |publisher=William S. Orr}}</ref>
*''Report on the Constitution and Operations of Life Assurance Societies'' (1841)<ref name="Ridpath"/>
*''A Manual of Map-making and Mechanical Geography'' (1846)<ref>{{Cite book |author= Jamieson, Alexander |title=A Manual of Map-making and Mechanical Geography: Illustrated by 60 Engravings: Comprising Projections of the Sphere, General and Particular Maps, and Topographical Plans, for the Purpose of Facilitating Practical Education, and the Operations of Land-surveying, Military and Naval Surveys |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v5EZAAAAYAAJ|year=1846|publisher=A. Fullarton and Company}}</ref>
*''Elements of Algebra''<ref name="CarrCarr2005"/>
